baseline_models.focus_anchor: The temporal deictic حِينَئِذٍ and the second-person plural تَنظُرُونَ.
baseline_models.mechanism: A specifically marked instant synchronizes a plurality of observers and directs their sight or attention toward an event present to them.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies the definite occasion that temporally pins the collective act.
The branch supplies directed visual or reflective attention as the group's activity.

changed_reading.before: A loose connective followed by a generic statement that the addressees look.
changed_reading.after: The clause stages a collective act of attention at one sharply indicated instant.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The shared waiting potential of حِينَئِذٍ and تَنظُرُونَ.
baseline_models.mechanism: The time-word can evoke awaiting an appointed occasion while the looking-root can evoke waiting or deferral, producing a held interval rather than a completed glance.

activation_trace.role: The branch contributes anticipation of the moment and makes the deictic time feel awaited.
The branch contributes expectant waiting and turns the ongoing look into temporal suspension.

changed_reading.before: The addressees simply see something at that time.
changed_reading.after: The addressees are held at the awaited moment, watching and waiting for what they cannot yet resolve.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surrounding sequence separates knowledge, protective concealment, touch, looking, and seeing. The focus gaze therefore registers real attention without guaranteeing access to the event's hidden layer.

activation_trace.role: Directed sight or reflection supplies the genuine but bounded act performed in the focus.
Disclosure to a knower establishes knowledge as a distinct level beyond mere looking.
Protective concealment supplies a hidden layer that ordinary observation need not penetrate.
Tactile contact adds another access mode and shows that access is differentiated rather than automatic.
Explicit ocular seeing, negated in its source construction, caps the sequence by marking the observers' visual limit.

structural_cues: The sequence moves from knowing in 56:76 through concealment and restricted touch in 56:78-79 to looking in 56:84 and explicit non-seeing in 56:85.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies distinct knowledge, concealment, touch, gaze, and negated sight; I infer a graded access sequence in which looking is real but insufficient. A live alternative is that each access term remains local to its own object.

changed_reading.before: Looking is equivalent to apprehending what is happening.
changed_reading.after: The observers attend to the visible crisis while its decisive dimension remains outside their sensory and epistemic reach.

context_deltas.mechanism: Arrival at a limit is localized in the throat, the conduit of breath and food. This gives حِينَئِذٍ an exact bodily threshold and activates its death-calamity branch, while تَنظُرُونَ positions the plural addressees as present observers.

activation_trace.role: The death or calamity branch makes the indicated instant specifically terminal rather than merely sequential.
Directed gaze places the addressed group at the threshold as immediate witnesses.
Reaching the endpoint supplies the terminal movement that defines when 'then' occurs.
The throat as the passage of breath and food gives that endpoint a precise bodily location.

structural_cues: The focus follows 56:83 without a new named event, so its temporal deictic points directly back to the reaching-throat construction.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies endpoint arrival and the throat conduit; I infer a terminal bodily passage and assign the plural addressees the role of onlookers rather than controllers. The narrower alternative is an unspecified acute bodily crisis.

changed_reading.before: The addressees look at some event at a marked time.
changed_reading.after: At the instant the crisis reaches its bodily endpoint in the throat, the addressees stand present and watch.

context_deltas.mechanism: The human group is near enough to direct its gaze, yet the next ayah asserts a still nearer presence that the group does not see. Spatial nearness and perceptual access are uncoupled.

activation_trace.role: The focus branch supplies the observers' active gaze and establishes the human side of the contrast.
Nearness contrary to distance introduces a presence closer than the visibly gathered observers.
Ocular sight, negated in the source, blocks the observers from converting physical proximity into perception.

structural_cues: The adjacent second-person plurals 'you look' and 'you do not see' form an immediate contrast across 56:84-85.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies human gaze, greater nearness, and negated sight; I infer that the decisive nearest presence is outside the group's visible field. Alternatively, the two sight verbs may differ only by local object rather than by depth of access.

changed_reading.before: The nearest witnesses are those visibly watching the scene.
changed_reading.after: The watching group discovers that physical attendance does not make it nearest or let it see the presence closest to the event.

context_deltas.mechanism: The following challenge links freedom from reckoning to the ability to return what has reached the threshold and demands truth in action. Watching becomes evidence of non-sovereignty: the group can attend but cannot reverse.

activation_trace.role: Directed attention supplies the passive capability that is contrasted with the demanded intervention.
Reckoning and requital frame the scene as a test of the claim to be beyond imposed consequence.
Restoration to the prior state supplies the concrete action the observers are challenged to perform.
Truth realized in deed makes successful reversal the proposed verification rather than verbal assertion.

structural_cues: The repeated challenge form in 56:83 and 56:86 encloses the looking clause, and the second-person plural continues into the return-command of 56:87.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies reckoning, a demand for restoration, and truth verified by action; I infer that the unanswered challenge exposes inability and recasts watching as enforced passivity. Alternatively, the challenge tests a claim without semantically redefining the gaze.

changed_reading.before: The group happens to be passive while it observes.
changed_reading.after: Its very spectatorship demonstrates the boundary of its power: it can watch the threshold but cannot restore what is passing beyond it.

context_deltas.mechanism: The single marked moment is followed by three alternative classifications and contrasting receptions. حِينَئِذٍ becomes a common threshold before divergent social and consequential paths, without implying that the human observers can see those paths.

activation_trace.role: The definite occasion supplies the shared temporal hinge from which the later alternatives unfold.
Privileged nearness supplies one classified relation on the far side of the threshold.
Blessed fortune supplies the positive quality of a second classified group.
Deviation from the intended path supplies the negative quality of the third classified group.
Prepared reception turns classification into an ensuing consequence rather than a bare label.
Reality fixed against falsehood seals the alternatives as consequential rather than hypothetical scenery.

structural_cues: The repeated alternative openings in 56:88, 56:90, and 56:92 divide the aftermath into three cases immediately after the challenge sequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a marked focus time followed by three classified outcomes; I infer that the time functions as their common threshold. A live alternative is that the classifications concern only the person at the center and add no semantic load to the focus deictic.

changed_reading.before: The focus marks one undifferentiated moment of watching.
changed_reading.after: It marks the shared threshold at which one visible crisis opens into sharply divergent aftermaths that the watchers themselves do not necessarily perceive.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The custodial branch is form-distant from the finite verb, so this is not a grammatical claim that the addressees are official guards. It remains anchored in the focus looking-root and gains a coherent spatial contrast from the nearer unseen presence; downstream prose should present it only as an exploratory role-image.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: تَنظُرُونَ can activate the looking-root's image of a watcher who observes and guards.

activation_trace.role: The branch recasts the gathered observers as would-be custodians who can watch but not preserve the passage.
Greater nearness displaces the human watchers from the position of closest attendance.
Negated ocular sight limits even the would-be custodians' knowledge of what they attend.

changed_reading.before: The addressees are emotionally neutral spectators.
changed_reading.after: They resemble displaced watchers: physically attending and perhaps trying to guard the person, yet neither closest to nor perceptually master of the passage.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: Reversing the gaze's agency is syntactically surprising because the second-person plural remains the explicit actor. The image is still anchored in the death branches of both focus roots and in the reached-throat context; downstream prose must keep the humans' literal looking primary and label the counter-gaze as poetic branch resonance.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: حِينَئِذٍ carries a death-calamity branch while تَنظُرُونَ carries the image of time's destructive glance.

activation_trace.role: The branch loads the indicated time with the arrival of death or calamity.
The branch supplies the startling counter-image of time looking upon people and overtaking them.
Arrival at the endpoint gives the counter-image an event boundary rather than leaving it free-floating.
The throat conduit bodily anchors the terminal event that seems to look back at its observers.

changed_reading.before: Only the human group directs a gaze at the terminal scene.
changed_reading.after: Alongside that literal gaze, a contained poetic counter-image lets the death-marked time itself seem to have looked upon and overtaken the scene.

strongest_changes: The preceding reached-throat construction turns a generic 'then' into an exact terminal bodily threshold.
The adjacent contrast between looking and not seeing makes human observation genuine but radically incomplete.
The demand to restore what has reached the threshold converts passive watching into evidence of limited control and exposure to reckoning.
The later three-way outcomes make the one witnessed moment a common hinge before divergent aftermaths.
summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah couples two roots that each contain both ordinary and terminal or expectant branches. Context activates those latent edges while preserving the plain scene: a gathered group truly looks, yet its gaze neither reaches the nearest presence nor grants power to reverse the event.
remaining_uncertainties: The waiting senses of both focus roots may be resonance rather than active meaning in the finite construction.
The later classifications may sharpen the temporal threshold without belonging to what the observers themselves witness.
The custodial and counter-gaze outliers are useful role-images but should not be promoted to direct lexical glosses.
